elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause still binds Customer: "During the term of this Agreement, and in no event beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date, neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory a product, other than a Product, that includes Binimetinib or Encorafenib as an active pharmaceutical ingredient." A narrowed covenant is still a restriction, so the preferred (no restriction at all) level is not reached.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Ono is deleted from the class-based prohibition (opening sentence now reads "neither Array nor its Controlled Affiliates"), and the only covenant binding Ono reads on "a product, other than a Product, that includes Binimetinib or Encorafenib as an active pharmaceutical ingredient" "" i.e. the two expressly defined, named compounds (Sections 1.2 and 1.17), not the redacted compound class. The Ono-side grant-to-licensee/distributor extension and the redacted-class trigger no longer apply to Customer.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: The covenant is expressly framed "During the term of this Agreement", and the former post-termination extension ("prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect", triggered by Section 13.3 or Section 13.2 termination) is deleted in its entirety. No post-term tail on Customer remains anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Outer cap stated in operative language: "and in no event beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date". The cap is a hard twelve-month limit, so the restriction cannot exceed 12 months even if the term is longer; it does not exceed the fallback numeric threshold.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: "This Section 8.2 shall not restrict (i) Ono's or its Affiliates' internal research or Development activities" "" an express carve-out in operative text, not merely promised in the comment.
"... or (ii) any product or program acquired by Ono or its Affiliates through any acquisition of or merger with a Third Party." Acquired products and programs are carved out of the covenant.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: all five fallback elements appear in operative language (named compounds only, in-term only, hard 12-month cap, internal development carve-out, acquisition carve-out). Preferred is not met because a narrowed covenant still binds Customer "" that is the expected outcome for a fallback-targeted redline.

Minimality holds. Removing Ono from the opening class-based prohibition is required for element 1; deleting the post-termination extension is required for elements 2 and 3; the cap and the two carve-outs are each required by a selected element. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added.

Conforming Array's termination trigger from "Commercializes a Competing Product in the Ono Territory during [ * ]" to "Commercializes a product in breach of this Section 8.2" is necessary rather than gratuitous: "Competing Product" now describes only Array's class-wide restriction, so the retained sentence would otherwise let Array terminate for conduct Ono is no longer prohibited from. The dropped "in the Ono Territory" and "during [ * ]" qualifiers are subsumed by the narrowed covenant, which is itself territory-, term- and 12-month-limited, so Array's right is not expanded in substance.

Intent is preserved: Array's reciprocal class-wide restriction and the redacted trigger binding Array are untouched, the royalty-termination consequence for Array's own Competing Product commercialization survives with the "Competing Product" definition still operative in clauses (i)/(ii), and the definitional tail ([ * ] meanings and the avoidance-of-doubt sentence) is retained. No dangling cross-reference is created "" Section 8.2 continues to exist for the Article XIV reference, and the deleted Section 13.2/13.3 references were part of the removed post-term extension only.

Drafting note only (not a defect): the cap is anchored to "the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date" rather than to the start of the covenant. That is acceptable because it can only shorten the restriction, but if the parties expect the covenant to bite from a later commercialization date, consider "twelve (12) months from the Effective Date" language being restated as the shorter of the term or twelve (12) months to avoid argument.
